g.text: Book Ch. 12, Sec. 12.3.1 · will enough light survive the chip to be detected? Add up every loss, then compare with what the detector needs

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 10.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #64d2ff

g.text: 1 · Follow the light: every stage costs some power

text.style: font-size: 8.2px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: the budget must include ALL losses: optical interface losses, measured waveguide losses, insertion losses of on-chip devices, etc.

g.text: Takeaway: subtract every loss in dB. 0 dBm − 6 − 10 − 6 dB = −22 dBm: 2 dB short of a −20 dBm 10 Gb/s receiver,

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: but far above the −80 dBm that device characterisation (particularly at low frequency) can measure.

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 7.8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Book Sec. 12.3.1 “Optical power budgets” (p. 400). Light path is schematic; the 2 dB / 58 dB margins, EDFA lift and mW values are our arithmetic from the book’s numbers.
